title: Tech Note: Elevated Privileges on macOS using sudo
author: Timothy Aaron Penner, Senior Technical Services Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note is about a standard Unix/macOS administration technique (configuring /etc/sudoers for passwordless privilege elevation) rather than a 4D-specific feature, so the underlying concept remains accurate today, though Apple's security hardening (SIP, notarization, Gatekeeper) has tightened around what elevated commands can actually accomplish on modern macOS versions since 2018. The 4D-side mechanism for invoking shell commands from 4D code is still valid.
related_updates: /etc/sudoers configuration technique is unchanged as a general macOS/Unix mechanism
macOS has added further security restrictions (SIP, notarization) since 2018 that may limit what elevated commands can do even with passwordless sudo
4D's external process/shell command invocation commands remain in the language
